Subject: TraceLens: LangChain shim + low-overhead tracing — quick proposal

Hi Mina,

Quick intro — I'm Samir, Head of Integrations at PromptWeave. We built TraceLens, a lightweight tracing shim for LangChain agents that emits span-like events optimized for token-level tracing without shipping full OTLP on every call. PromptWeave is seeing interest from platform teams who want fine-grained call tracing and prompt-level attribution with <5% p50 latency overhead.

We'd love to pilot TraceLens with Redwood as an optional instrumentation path in your LangChain SDK compatibility layer. Main value props:
- Low overhead: sampled token traces + adaptive batching
- Easy dev experience: single-line enable in pw-langkit, automatic span tags for model, prompt_hash, route
- Optional bridge to OpenTelemetry collectors for customers that need full telemetry

Attached is a short integration proposal, a tiny demo bundle, and a sample patch that shows the shim hooking into LangChain's agent loop.

Would you and your integrations team be open to a 30-minute run-through next week? Suggested agenda: demo (10m), integration surface (10m), pilot success criteria & timeline (10m).

Thanks — excited to explore.

Samir Rao

- Sampling: how is sampling configured (probabilistic, adaptive latency-based)? Can Redwood control sampling policy per-route?

Subject: Re: TraceLens: LangChain shim + low-overhead tracing — follow-up and materials

Thanks all — quick answers inline:
- Format: TraceLens emits per-turn spans with optional token deltas. Default is per-turn spans (start/end, token_count, prompt_hash) and an opt-in token-stream mode for sampling token payloads. We map core fields to OTEL names (trace_id, span_id, name, attributes) and include "pw.prompt_hash" and "pw.model_variant" as vendor attributes.
- Sampling: supports probabilistic and adaptive (latency-triggered). We expose policy control via env or SDK config and can honor an external sampling policy endpoint (so Redwood can centrally control sampling per-route).
- Backpressure: default behavior is local ring-buffer + async flush; we can switch to drop-oldest or backpressure the generator. Benchmarking shows ~3.5% p50 overhead and ~6% p95 overhead for token-stream mode on a 16k-context run on a 80GB GPU instance (numbers in attached perf sheet).
- Integration UX: pw-langkit supports an import-time enable flag (environment toggle) and also a no-code compatibility shim that maps Redwood's LangChain hooks to TraceLens calls.

I'll bring Alex (our engineering lead) to the Jan 21 demo and share the short security note and perf slide before the meeting (sending now as attachments and the GitHub link above). Proposed pilot: 4-week POC with a single Redwood test route, success criteria: no >1% increase in 95th latency at production load (with token-stream disabled by default), accurate prompt attribution for 95% of traced turns, and successful export to a customer OTLP collector.

Looking forward to the call — Samir
